texts.preamble: Muhammed Sabir vs Food Safety Officer on 23 August, 2024 Author: P.V.Kunhikrishnan Bench: P.V.Kunhikrishnan Crl.M.C. Nos.6319 of 2017 & 2464 of 2018 1 2024:Ker:65531 In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present The Honourable Mr. Justice P.V.Kunhikrishnan Friday, The 23Rd Day Of August 2024 / 1St Bhadra, 1946 Crl.Mc No. 6319 Of 2017 Against The Order/Judgment Dated In St No.1030 Of 2016 Of Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - Ii, Kothamangalam Petitioner/2Nd Accused: S.M.Muhammed S/O.Moideen, Aged 60 Years, Residing At Srambickal House,Eastern Valley, Machiplavu P.O Adimali, Idukki District,Pin - 685 561 By Advs. Sri.Santhosh Subramanian Sri.Sherry J. Thomas Sri.S.Sreekumarnorth Paravur Sri.E.A.Thankappan Respondents/Complainant & State: 1 Food Safety Officer, Kothamangalam Circle,Ernakulam District - 686 693 2 State Of Kerala Represented By Public Prosecutor,High Court Of Kerala, Eernakulam, Pin - 682 031 By Adv. Sri.Grashious Kuriakose, Adgp, Sri.Renjith.T.R, Sr.Pp
texts.facts: 2. Petitioner is the 2nd accused in S.T.No.1030/2016 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - II, Kothamangalam. The above case is registered alleging offences punishable under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. On 18.02.2015 at about 3.45 p.m., the 1 st respondent, Food Safety Officer of Kothamangalam Circle visited Crl.M.C. Nos.6319 of 2017 & 2464 of 2018 2024:KER:65531 the warehouse of M/s. Eastern Chai (Pvt) Ltd. and in the store room of the company 1000 kg of tea dust was seen packed in 250 grams each sealed and labeled packets and from the said stock 8 packets of 250 grams each tea dust was taken as sample by the 1 st respondent. From those 8 packets, two packets each, were tied together, and four sample units were prepared by the 1st respondent and from such sample units, one sample unit was sent for chemical analysis to the Regional Analytical Laboratory, Ernakulam and a report was received and based on the same, Annexure-I complaint was filed. Annexure-II is the food analyst report in Form B. As per Annexure-II, the tea dust contains iron filings which is quantified at 592.25 mg/Kg and as per the report, iron filing shall be absent. Being aggrieved by the opinion expressed by the food analyst in Annexure-II report, another part Crl.M.C. Nos.6319 of 2017 & 2464 of 2018 2024:KER:65531 of the sample was sent on the request of the petitioner to the Referral Laboratory, Kolkotta and a report in Form A was received as evident by Annexure-III. In column No.8 of Annexure-III report, it is stated that iron filings detected at 1378.39 mg/Kg. As per the report, iron filings shall be absent. Hence it is alleged that the accused committed the offence. 3. Crl.M.C. No.2464/2018 is filed to quash the proceedings in S.T. No. 1534/2017 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - III, Kottayam. In this case also, the prosecution is as per the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. It is stated that the tea dust seized as per Annexure-II was sent for analysis, and the analyst reported that there is iron filing. According to the petitioners, even if the entire allegations are accepted, no offence Crl.M.C. Nos.6319 of 2017 & 2464 of 2018 2024:KER:65531 is made out. Hence these Criminal Miscellaneous Cases are filed. The short point raised by the petitioners is that, in the light of the order dated 17.08.2023 in Crl.M.C. No.7955/2017, the prosecution against the petitioners is to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. "The petitioner herein is the 2nd accused in Crl.M.C. Nos.6319 of 2017 & 2464 of 2018 2024:KER:65531 S.T.No. 831 of 2016 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate-I, Idukki. In the aforesaid case, he is facing prosecution for having committed offences punishable under Section3.1 (zz) (iii) & (xi), 26 2(i), 27(i) and 59(i) of FSS Act, 2006 r/w. Regulation No. 2.10.1:(1) of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standard and Food Additives) Regulations 2011. 2. The prosecution alleges that on 12.02.2016, at approximately 3.30 PM, an inspection was conducted at Door No.III/165-A shop namely Sneha Agencies of Idukki-Kanjikuzhy Grama Panchayath, and 2 kg of tea were seized for analysis by the food analyst. The samples were analyzed by the Food Analyst of the Regional Analytical Laboratory, Kakkanad. As per the report, the sample contains extraneous matter (iron filings) to the extent of not less than 191.35 mg per kg, which is in excess of the safe limit, and hence the food was categorised as unsafe.
texts.arguments: 3. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, through its Director (RCD) had issued Annexure- IV order dated 02.11.2017, whereby directions were issued to the States not to launch prosecution for non-conformance of the limit of iron filings for cases where samples were picked up/tested prior to 19.05.2016. Directions were Crl.M.C. Nos.6319 of 2017 & 2464 of 2018 2024:KER:65531 also issued to withdraw all such prosecutions launched prior to 19.05.2016, either under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 or under the PFA Act, 1954. The learned counsel submits that in identical circumstances, this Court had [LEAKAGE_MASK] the proceedings against the accused by order dated 05.02.2018 in Crl. M.C.No.3248 of 2017. 4. The learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the submissions. He points out that even as of date, the upper limit of iron filings permitted in tea has not been finalized by the Food Safety Authority.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 3. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, through its Director (RCD) had issued Annexure- IV order dated 02.11.2017, whereby directions were issued to the States not to launch prosecution for non-conformance of the limit of iron filings for cases where samples were picked up/tested prior to 19.05.2016. Directions were Crl.M.C. Nos.6319 of 2017 & 2464 of 2018 2024:KER:65531 also issued to withdraw all such prosecutions launched prior to 19.05.2016, either under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 or under the PFA Act, 1954. The learned counsel submits that in identical circumstances, this Court had [LEAKAGE_MASK] the proceedings against the accused by order dated 05.02.2018 in Crl. M.C.No.3248 of 2017. 4. The learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the submissions. He points out that even as of date, the upper limit of iron filings permitted in tea has not been finalized by the Food Safety Authority.
